Complete and interpolate a time series

Source: R/interpolate_series.R
interpolate_series.Rd

Completes the calendar grid of one or more series and interpolates missing values inside the observed span. Missing periods that are absent from the input are made explicit before interpolation, so later observations remain attached to the correct dates.

Leading and trailing missing values are not extrapolated. By default, a Kalman smoother is attempted first and linear interpolation is used if the state-space model cannot be estimated.

Usage

interpolate_series(
  data,
  date_col = "date",
  value_col = "value",
  group_cols = NULL,
  frequency = NULL,
  method = "auto",
  max_gap = NULL,
  imputed_col = FALSE,
  .quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame, tibble, or data.table.

date_col

Name of the date column. It must have class Date.

value_col

Name of one or more numeric value columns.

group_cols

Optional character vector identifying separate series.

frequency

Observations per year. Supported values are 1, 2, 4, 12, 52, and 365. When NULL, the frequency is inferred from the dates.

method

Interpolation method. One of "auto", "kalman", "linear", or "spline". "auto" tries a structural time-series Kalman smoother and falls back to linear interpolation if the model cannot be estimated; "kalman" errors instead. Both keep the Kalman estimates, with a warning, when the model fit does not converge.

max_gap

Maximum consecutive missing periods to interpolate. NULL uses floor(0.75 * n), where n is the span from the first through the last observed value. Use Inf to remove the limit.

imputed_col

If TRUE, add one logical column per value column named imputed_{value_col}. A flag is true only where a value was filled.

.quiet

If TRUE, suppress fallback, non-convergence, date-normalization, and high missingness warnings.

Value

A tibble on a complete date grid. Value columns are interpolated in place; leading and trailing missing values remain NA. Rows are ordered by group and date.

Details

The Kalman method estimates a basic structural model with stats::StructTS() when there are at least two observed seasonal cycles. Annual, weekly, and daily series, and seasonal series with fewer observations, use a local linear trend model. Only missing observations are replaced; observed values are never smoothed.

Linear and cubic spline interpolation use stats::approx() and stats::spline(), respectively. Cubic splines can overshoot around sharp changes, so linear interpolation is the fallback used by method = "auto".

Calendar conventions are detected separately within each group. Consistent period starts, period ends, weekdays, and within-period calendar positions are preserved. Inconsistent conventions are normalized to period starts.

Examples

monthly <- data.frame(
  date = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2020-02-01", "2020-04-01")),
  value = c(1, 2, 4)
)

interpolate_series(monthly, frequency = 12, method = "linear")
#> # A tibble: 4 × 2
#>   date       value
#>   <date>     <dbl>
#> 1 2020-01-01     1
#> 2 2020-02-01     2
#> 3 2020-03-01     3
#> 4 2020-04-01     4
interpolate_series(
  monthly,
  frequency = 12,
  method = "linear",
  imputed_col = TRUE
)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   date       value imputed_value
#>   <date>     <dbl> <lgl>        
#> 1 2020-01-01     1 FALSE        
#> 2 2020-02-01     2 FALSE        
#> 3 2020-03-01     3 TRUE         
#> 4 2020-04-01     4 FALSE
